text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- German current affairs magazine Focus quoted Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel as saying Bundesbank head Hans Tietmeyer "a right pig" during a press breakfast in Amsterdam. Focus called Schuessel an unpredictable risk in the government.

- Italian-dominated insurer EA Generali has set its sights on an alliance with Die Erste Oesterreichischen Sparcasse after failing in its bid to buy the government's stake in Creditanstalt-Bankverein earlier this year.
- Optimism in the Austrian population is climbing again for the first time in over two years, a survey for Der Standard said.
- The Liberal Forum attacked government plans to bug private mobile phones, which it estimates will cost around 300 million schillings.
- A new gun law comes into effect on Tuesday in line with European Union regulations. Prospective gun owners will now have to undergo psychological tests.
- Economic institute WIFO warns Austria is not exploiting new technology to the full and could hinder its chances of growth.
- The Second European Ecumenical Conference in Graz ended on Sunday, amid calls for reconciliation, despite earlier accusations of proselytism particularly by the Roman Catholic Church in the East.
- Civil servants will negotiate in the next three weeks on the next steps to be taken in their protest at salary cuts and staff reductions and want long-term reforms agreed by mid September.
- Bawag is parting company with paper company Steyrermuehl and will sell the remaining 20 percent in the next days. Last year it sold a majority stake in the firm to German Haindl Group.
- Die Erste chief Konrad Fuchs says the firm aims to turn the bank into a private quality bank once the merger with GiroCredit has been completed.
- Vienna mayor Michael Haeupl says he opposes a premature debate on the next holder of the Austrian presidency out of respect for current President Thomas Klestil.
- The rate of insolvencies in Austria has begun to decline in the first half of 1997, according to the Credit Protection agency.
- High-grade steelmaker Boehler Uddeholm wants to buy Thyssen holding EWK and French steel firm Usinor.
